messages:
irina: Heads-up — nightly apples-to-apples kernel-selection CI job tripped a perf alert this morning on staging. p99 is ~12% worse than our baseline for the same model+sequence config. job: nightly/perf/kernel-selection-2026-03-16

irina: Log snippet and the assertion that failed:
```
[03:12:10] bench: model: redwood-7b-fp16, seq=1024, batch=8
[03:12:10] metrics: p50=8.2ms p95=45.6ms p99=198.4ms
[03:12:10] baseline: p99=177.0ms, regression=21.4ms (12.1%)
[03:12:10] assert regression < 0.08  # threshold 8%
AssertionError: regression 0.121 > 0.08
```

matt: Ugh. Do we know if this is driven by kernel selection changes or by variations in batching distribution? Any recent merges? Can you paste the exact replay command so I can run locally?

irina: replay command I used:
```bash
./harness/replay --trace s3://perf-traces/kernel-selection/2026-03-15/trace.tar.gz --model redwood-7b-fp16 --seq 1024 --batch 8 --no-cache-warmup --emit-metrics=prom
```
Note: I disabled cache warmup to match baseline job config.

kai: I merged the dynamic-batching heuristic tweak last night (PR #4123) — it changes target queue depth heuristics when instance utilization > 85%. Could be increasing micro-variance in request coalescing. Reverting is quick if we confirm.

lauren: CI signal looks noisy: last week's nightly had 2 other transient spikes but those were within the flaky window and auto-muted. This one crossed the configured 'hard' threshold. I recommend doing a gated triage:
- 1) reproduce locally with the same harness and trace
- 2) run three consecutive CI runs to rule out single-night noise
- 3) compare kernel selection logs (`kernel_choice` events) side-by-side

matt: I'm on it. Running replay now (starting 1801209908). If it's the batch heuristic, the kernel selector could pick a different matmul kernel for smaller tail batches which hits a pathological path. I'll diff the `kernel_choice` entries.

irina: I pushed a quick perf dashboard snapshot (Grafana) to the perf-dashboard channel: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/sel123/kernel-selection-nightly — includes per-kernel latency breakdowns and queue depth heatmap.

ci-bot: [automated] Perf alert created: perf-regression-1801209876. linked job nightly/perf/kernel-selection-2026-03-16. Severity=high. Notified: #eng-runtime, #eng-oncall.

matt: First local run: p99 matches CI (~196ms). Digging into kernel_choice. Quick paste of interesting lines:
```
kernel_choice: batch=8, seq=1024, chosen_kernel=matmul_fast_8x128, fallback=matmul_generic, kv_cache_hit=false
kernel_choice: batch=3, seq=1024, chosen_kernel=matmul_generic, reason=low_queue_depth
```
Looks like increased churn in batch sizes leads to more `matmul_generic` fallbacks for some shards. That kernel has worse perf for our sequence length.

kai: That aligns with my heuristic change: we now occasionally start shards at lower target batch to reduce latency for small bursts, which can increase generic-kernel use. Two options: tighten the heuristic to prefer fast kernels when seq>512, or add an architecture-level affinity so the kernel selector prefers `matmul_fast_*` when model dims match.

lauren: For CI automation, proposal: instead of firing immediately on a single-night breach, have CI create a blocked issue and require 2/3 consecutive nightly confirmations to auto-escalate to high-severity. Also add an automated kernel_choice diff task that uploads a small TSV to the perf bucket so triage is easier.

irina: Agreed. Short term I'd like to mute the hard alert and run 3 extra reruns tonight so we can confirm root cause before reverting code. I'll add a note to the CI run: `reason=investigate-kernel-choice-noise`.

matt: If we implement kernel selector affinity fix, add a microbench that exercises `matmul_fast_8x128` vs `matmul_generic` at seq=1024 and small batch sizes so CI can catch regressions independent of the full replay harness.

lauren: I'll update the flaky-triage doc and CI job config:
- add `--retries 3` for nightly/perf jobs (only for regression detection, not gating)
- upload `kernel_choice.diff` artifact on failure
- publish dashboard snapshot URL in the created issue

irina: Thanks. I'll queue the 3 reruns and paste results later. If we see same behavior across reruns we'll rollback the batching heuristic PR and cut a follow-up with the kernel affinity change.

matt: thx, looping in @kai for the follow-up PR. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: [automated] Rerun queued: nightly/perf/kernel-selection-2026-03-16 (attempt 2 of 3).
